name: level1-lose-ecology
description: Level 1 losing scenario: massive blasts with max krackle, triggering ecology score collapse and, after a sustained 150-tick zero streak, the government shutdown that actually ends the level (ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS, EcologicalDisaster.ts). depth:6 (not the originally-declared 12) throughout: the Drill panel's real click always uses its own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M regardless of what a scenario's command field declares, a new sub-class of Finding #3/#4 caught only by a real interaction-mode run (see the note on the first blast step). With the corrected, shallower/more-violent holes, ecology bottoms out at exactly 0 after just the SECOND blast (not the fifth), and the file's own original tick budget already ticks past the 150-consecutive-ticks-at-zero threshold -- the shutdown this file is named for now fires for real, no extension needed.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:5 cols:5 spacing:3 depth:6 start:5,5

expect.note: spacing:3 already matches the Drill panel's own default (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3, Drill.ts) -- the (5,5)-(17,17) drag is a 12-unit span, round(12/3)+1=5, so the row/col/spacing part of the grid was already correct. depth was not: corrected from the originally-declared 12 to 6, the panel's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M -- caught only by a real interaction-mode run, which failed with ecology 14.47 instead of the depth:12 command-mode trace's 48.99 (shallower holes with the same charge concentrate energy over less rock, producing far more violent fragmentation/projections). A new sub-class of Finding #3/#4: the grid tool's real defaults extend to depth, not just row/col/spacing -- every prior file's `drill_plan grid` fix only ever checked hole COUNT, which depth doesn't affect, so this class could be silently present in already-completed files too; flagged in the plan doc as a follow-up audit item.
